title.narrative: RSS/NERC - MENA NEXUS initiativ för förnyelsebar energi tekniker
RSS/NERC - MENA Region Initiative - a NEXUS Approach & Renewable Energy Tech

description.narrative:
RSS/NERC has applied for funding of 48 000 000 MSEK to carry out the programme "The MENA Region Intiative as a Model of NEXUS Approach and Renewable Energy Technologies " during the period 2016-2019.
The intervention aims to enhance the capacity of MENA Municipalities as local authorities to promote needed reforms and innovations in the field of Sustainable Development and Green Economy, by boosting resilience to current climate variability through the use of ren energy and energy efficiency applications, saving water and enhance institutional strengthening of the relevant government authorities.

Royal Scientific Society/National Energy Research Center (RSS/NERC) har ansökt till Sida om stöd på 48 MSEK för att genomföra projektet "The MENA Region Initiative as a model of NEXUS Approach and Renewable Energy Technologies" i MENA regionen med ett fokus på länderna Jordanien, Libanon och Tunisien under perioden 2017-2020.
Den föreslagna insatsen syftar till att stärka kapaciteten hos kommuner i MENA regionen vad gäller hållbar utveckling och "grön ekonomi" genom att stärka motståndskraften mot klimatförändringar genom ökad användning av förnybar energi och åtgärder för att förbättra energieffektivitet. Förbättringar inom dessa områden kommer också att leda till en förbättrad och mer effektiv vattenanvändning.
Insatsens totala budget är 50.5 MSEK och organisationens eget bidrag är 2.5 MSEK.

Strengthen regional cooperation within the MENA region through implementing NEXUS approach, integrating plans for renewable energy, energy efficiency, water management and food production tools at each municipalitys level, to combat poverty, provide opportunities for women, youth and other marginalized groups (including refugees), and alleviate climate change effects.

Sida assesses the project has, to large extent, achieved the planned objectives and addressed the needs of the beneficiaries. Next are some examples of the results achieved:
- MINARET supported the municipalities of Al-Karak, Monastir, and Jdaidet el Chouf to join the Covenant of Mayors by providing technical support in identification of solutions for reduction of CO2 emissions by improving energy efficiency and renewable energy use. The preparation of the BEI (Baseline Emission Inventory) and the SEAP (Sustainable Energy Action Plan) / SECAP (Sustainable Energy and Climate Action Plan) based on the Covenant of Mayors methodology linked to the establishment of task forces in the municipalities will contribute to continued impact of the project in the municipalities and beyond them.
- The project made a measurable and significant difference in the longer term by empowering municipal workers to tackle issues of water, energy and food/ecosystems; embedding an understanding and appreciation for the importance of tackling NEXUS issues at local level; and providing a set of tools and skills to take NEXUS issues forward at municipal level. This last set of impacts is particularly important as a foundation to continue with municipalities to develop measures and implement activities in the future to tackle resource scarcity.
- Recent regional and international crisis (COVID-19 pandemic Lebanese financial and political crisis) added another layer of instability to the implementation of the pilot projects. Remarkably, beneficiaries in Lebanon felt that the project helped them endure the difficulties they faced. The water pilot project allowed more residents than expected to restore/harvest their degraded agricultural land during the lockdowns.
- The project gave special focus on women, disadvantaged groups and the poor. In Monastir the team of the NGO Voix de lEnfant informed that the support of the MINARET project was extremely timely and relevant in terms of providing disadvantaged women and their children with improved means to ensure their livelihoods. Furthermore, the water channel cleaning and installation of a solar powered water pump (i.e. Water Pilot Project) in addition to supplementing the power generation of Jdeideh Womens Organisation with solar panels (i.e. Energy Pilot Project) were often singled out as essential in relieving two main baseline grievances: the scarcity of water in the area (especially in late summer) and the high costs of electricity procurement incurred by the municipality and the residents.
- The project has achieved a good visibility plan; as dedication of pages on different social media channels, project website was launched, and a branding toolkit was produced in order to ensure the projects ownership and special visual identity, maintaining periodic updates about MENARET news, activities and other related issues.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
